meaning.evidence: All facts kept: New Jersey and Oregon rules, "comes to 3.785 litres", pay before pump, "I need 50 bucks on pump number 1", octanes 87/89/91 and 85, red diesel, black versus green handles. Asides react to facts ("Short-changed from the get-go.", "where the air's thin"), but "wander inside past the pie that's been in the warmer since Tuesday" adds an invented scene.

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "flog it by the gallon", "servos", "shootin' through without payin'", "the folding stuff", "on the till", "sold out bush", "truckies", "some flash luxury number".

authenticity.evidence: Sounds like a real Aussie explaining America: "Bit of a palaver, but there ya go.", "Your Yank'll go", "Not worth it." Only "from the get-go" is American.

register.evidence: A full level-5 yarn, with "against the bloody law" and "make bloody sure" well inside vulgarity 2.

tone.evidence: The guide's practical, warning tone survives the chat: "And this is the one that'll catch ya out.", "So check the handle before ya squeeze, and don't mix 'em up."

flow.evidence: Reads aloud easily, varied sentence shapes: "Then there's the octane.", "Now here's one to watch". "the dosh ya handed over ... the dosh ya didn't use" repeats.

variety.evidence: Wide range of openers and terms: "True story, this.", "Now,", "Then there's", "Now here's one to watch", "flog", "shootin' through", "palaver", "dosh", "folding stuff".

essence.evidence: Still the Wikivoyage advice on US fuel, every point in order, told as a yarn.

A.summary: A lively, faithful level-5 yarn of the fuel guide with natural Aussie throughout; one invented aside and one Americanism.

meaning.evidence: Faithful point by point: "servos in the cities have to have at least 50% full-service pumps by law", "The pump'll cut out by itself", "shouldn't go in cars, cos there's hefty fines". Nothing lost.

sense.evidence: "servos", "okayed", "folding stuff", "dosh", "flash car", "out bush", "truckies" all fit. "Petrol ("gas")" quietly drops the point that 'gas' is what Americans call it.

authenticity.evidence: Natural, unforced: "near enough every American servo", "whoever's on the till", "ya have to get a credit or debit card okayed".

register.evidence: Steady Aussie voice but in the guide's sentence shapes, no swearing; more level 3-4 than a level-5 yarn.

tone.evidence: Informative tone kept exactly: "Don't mix 'em up."

flow.evidence: Smooth; some long run-ons kept from the original: "or ya can go back and get a refund of any dosh ya didn't use if ya guessed too high".

variety.evidence: Modest: "dosh" twice, "ya have to" repeated ("ya have to get", "ya have to guess").

problems.quote: These days, ya have to get a credit or debit card okayed at the pump first. Otherwise, ya have to guess
problems.original: Today, you have to preauthorize ... you have to estimate
problems.why: Lighter than the level-5 brief; stays close to the guide's structure.

B.summary: An accurate, natural Aussie version of the guide; restrained for level 5.

meaning.evidence: Mostly the original, but "I need 50 quid on pump number 1" turns the American's dollars into pounds, wrong in a passage about what Americans say.

sense.evidence: "quid" takes the wrong sense (British pounds, or dated Aussie money, not US dollars in an American's mouth); "Tell ya what, in the alternative" misuses the tag. "servos", "dosh" fit.

authenticity.evidence: Stage tags bolted onto officialese: "Jeez Louise, due to problems with frequent", "preauthorize a credit or debit card at the pump, cobber", "Streeeewth."; US "preauthorize" and "gas" left in.

register.evidence: Largely untranslated ("stations in urban areas are required by law to provide at least 50% full-service pumps"), with tags sprinkled; far below level 5.

tone.evidence: The guide's tone mostly kept, though the tags jar: "Don't mix them up. Streeeewth."

flow.evidence: Jarring joins: "Well, the American gallon is smaller", "Tell ya what, in the alternative, ya have to estimate", "identify which pump yer bloody using".

variety.evidence: Tags of one kind ("Listen", "Well", "Jeez Louise", "Tell ya what", "So anyway", "Streeeewth") and "dosh" twice.

essence.evidence: Recognisably the guide, since it is mostly the guide, but the pasted-on tags make it read as pastiche.

C.summary: The original with stage tags bolted on and a dollars-to-quid error; off the brief and jarring.

meaning.evidence: Every fact kept and in order: "self-serve's actually against the law", "it comes to 3.785 litres", "an American might go, \"I need 50 bucks on pump number 1\"", "So don't go mixin' 'em up."

sense.evidence: "servos", "okayed", "folding stuff", "dosh", "hirin' something flash", "out bush", "truckies" all fit.

authenticity.evidence: Natural spoken Aussie: "Mind you,", "Or else ya guess", "something flash", "So don't go mixin' 'em up."

register.evidence: Fully conversational Aussie, but no swearing and few yarning asides; a touch under the full level-5, vulgarity-2 weight.

tone.evidence: Informative and helpful throughout, the closing warning kept.

flow.evidence: Smooth, well-joined: "The pump cuts out by itself once the petrol hits the dosh ya handed over". Reads like it was written that way.

variety.evidence: Good spread of openers ("Over there", "Mind you", "Now,", "Then there's", "And"); "dosh" twice.

D.summary: A smooth, faithful, natural Aussie retelling; slightly restrained for level 5.

meaning.evidence: All points kept: "as the Yanks call it", "works out to 3.785 litres", "a Yank might say", "you'll cop a massive fine". The ending "or you'll be well and truly fucked" reacts to the warning.

sense.evidence: "servos", "on the counter", "flash luxury car", "out in the bush", "truckies", "cop a massive fine" fit. "Thanks to all the bloody \"drive offs\"" fits.

authenticity.evidence: Natural: "cop a massive fine", "make bloody sure", "well and truly fucked". "preauthorise" stays bureaucratic.

register.evidence: Aussie throughout with swearing up to the dial ("bloody", "fucked"), but the voice uses standard "you" and the guide's structure: level 4 more than a full yarn.

tone.evidence: The practical tone holds; the last-line swear sharpens the warning rather than flipping it: "Don't get 'em mixed up, or you'll be well and truly fucked."

flow.evidence: Clean, readable: "The pump cuts out by itself once the cost of the fuel hits the amount of cash you've handed over".

problems.quote: Don't get 'em mixed up, or you'll be well and truly fucked.
problems.why: The swear lands as a punchline the dry guide doesn't have; within the dial but a slight tonal lurch.

problems.quote: These days you've gotta preauthorise a credit or debit card at the pump.
problems.original: Today, you have to preauthorize a credit or debit card at the pump.
problems.why: Bureaucratic term kept where 'get it okayed' would sound natural.

E.summary: A clean, natural Aussie rendering with swearing at the dial; slightly under full yarn and a punchier ending.
